summary: On April 6, 2016, significant developments unfolded in both the corporate and legal arenas. Pharmaceutical giants Pfizer and Allergan called off their $160 billion merger following new U.S. Treasury regulations aimed at preventing tax inversions. This decision marked a major shift in corporate strategies concerning tax liabilities. Meanwhile, in a landmark legal case, former Massey Energy CEO Don Blankenship was sentenced to one year in prison for his role in the 2010 Upper Big Branch mine disaster, highlighting the accountability of corporate executives for safety violations. These stories underscored the impact of regulatory changes and legal accountability on corporate practices.

stories.headline: Pfizer, Allergan Scrap $160 Billion Merger
stories.summary: Pfizer Inc. and Allergan PLC terminated their $160 billion merger after the U.S. Treasury introduced new rules to curb tax inversions. The merger would have allowed Pfizer to relocate to Ireland for tax benefits, but the new regulations reduced the financial incentives. Both companies mutually agreed to abandon the deal, marking a significant shift in corporate tax strategy.

stories.headline: Ex-Massey CEO Sentenced for Mine Disaster
stories.summary: Don Blankenship, former CEO of Massey Energy, received a one-year prison sentence for conspiring to violate mine safety standards, leading to the 2010 Upper Big Branch mine disaster that killed 29 miners. This case marked a rare instance of a top executive being held criminally accountable for workplace safety violations. The sentencing was seen as a pivotal moment in corporate accountability.
